name: Osteochondral Lesion of the Talus
definition: Focal injury of talar articular cartilage and subchondral bone, often following ankle sprain or trauma and capable of causing persistent pain or locking.

typical: Persistent deep ankle pain after sprain

investigations.principle: MRI is sensitive for cartilage/subchondral injury; CT defines bony architecture; radiographs may miss small lesions.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Unstable or persistent symptomatic lesions may require arthroscopic repair/restoration.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Gulpha Asthi-Sandhi phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Focal injury of talar articular cartilage and subchondral bone, often following ankle sprain or trauma and capable of causing persistent pain or locking.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
